how_the_figures_were_obtained: PIPELINE_V2 section 3 says to check for publisher figure rasters before rendering anything. The main-article figures were NOT in source/ and the per-lipidoid values live only in them, so they had to be acquired. Three URL patterns were tried with a plain client and no user-agent spoofing: europepmc.org/api/fulltextRepo (403), /pmc/articles/PMC11368637/bin/<f>.jpg (404), and /articles/instance/11368637/bin/<f>.jpg (200). The third is the PMC author-manuscript asset route and serves 300 dpi JPEGs to an ordinary request, no browser and no session. The PMC OA service (oa.fcgi) 404s for this PMCID, which is expected: an NIH author manuscript is not in the standard OA subset. The article's own PDF at /articles/instance/11368637/pdf/nihms-2006250.pdf returns an HTML interstitial, not a PDF, so the JPEGs are the highest-fidelity form of the figures reachable without a browser.
what_was_NOT_obtained: The Wiley version-of-record PDF and its figure assets. The Wiley figures would be the publisher's own rasters; the PMC ones are the NIH author-manuscript deposit of the same figures. PIPELINE_V2 says Wiley needs a browser; no browser was used here because the PMC route already gave 300 dpi.

NIHMS2006250-supplement-1.pdf, the PMC-side copy of the Supporting Information. The Wiley .docx in source/ is the same material in its original form, and the .docx is strictly better (Tables S1-S3 are live Word tables, not pixels).
